title: console-observability-triage-scratchpad-samir-rao-2026-03-04
content:
Quick triage scratchpad — console / observability
Date: 2026-03-04
Owner: Samir Rao
Context: morning triage, customers reported flaky dashboard load + missing metrics for certain models. Inbox + #observability.

Observations:
- Multiple reports (internal slack + customer email) about the 'Per-Model Latency' dashboard showing large gaps between 02:15–02:45 UTC. Some panels return 500.
- Alerts: alert OBS-DASH-ERR (5x errors in dashboard-renderer) fired at 02:18 for ap-southeast region, suppressed at 02:55 after partial restart.
- Customer-reported: AcmePayments reported missing embeddings throughput chart from 02:00–03:00; they flagged SLA discrepancy.
- Related: a recent console change merged yesterday (PR #3821) touched the timeseries aggregation code — possible culprit.

Quick repro / facts:
- Dashboard load error reproduces for me on staging when time range > 24h AND querying "model:*-quantized" tags -> stack trace shows 502 from timeseries-backend.
- Timeseries-backend logs around 02:20 show repeated "kv-cache-miss" spikes and high GC pauses on node ts-03 (ap-southeast).
- ts-03 metrics: 85% CPU, heap growth, many blocked threads. Node restarted automatically by k8s at 02:47 (oomkilled?). Need to check pod events.

Immediate next actions (priority order):
1) Lock down customer comms: ping CS to let AcmePayments know we are triaging (Taylor). Leave short note: "Investigating missing dashboard metrics — likely infrastructure issue, ETA 1h".
2) Check pod events on ts-03 and capture logs (Samir) — grep for OOM, GC, or kernel OOM.
3) Revert or rollback PR #3821 on staging if we can reproduce consistently (Emily to coordinate rollback test).
4) Add short-term dashboard fallback: if timeseries-backend returns 5xx, surface cached snapshots and don't propagate 500 to UI (small UX fix, low-risk). Create ticket JIRA-OBS-2150.
5) Run health-checks across ts cluster to find other nodes with similar memory pressure (Owen).

Notes to self / debugging checklist:
- [ ] Capture full ts-03 pod logs (k8s: kubectl -n observability logs ts-03 --since=4h) -> save to /tmp/ts03-logs.txt
- [ ] kubectl describe pod ts-03 -> look for OOMKilled vs crashloopbackoff events
- [ ] Check JVM/heap dump retention config on timeseries-backend (recent change in PR #3780?)
- [ ] Confirm whether recent rollout included any config changes to aggregation window sizes (might blow up memory)
- [ ] Re-run query against timeseries-backend directly (curl timeseries/api/v1/query?...) with the problematic filter to see raw response/latency
- [ ] If reproduces, create mitigation: reduce default aggregation window for "model:*-quantized" queries to 1h for ap-southeast

Customer follow-ups (explicit):
- AcmePayments (acct: acme-payments): assign CS follow-up + include timeline and mitigation steps (Taylor)
- BetaCorp: they DM'd about slow page render; ask them for exact time + panel id (Emily)

Longer-term / postmortem ideas:
- Add canary checks for timeseries-backend that simulate worst-case queries (long time windows + many model tags) to detect memory blowups before rollout.
- Add circuit-breaker in UI to fallback to cached data when backend latency > 5s or 5xx.
- Revisit memory limits and JVM tuning for ts instances in ap-southeast; maybe bump to N+1.
- Add a quick dashboard to show node-level GC/pause metrics aggregated by cluster and recent restarts.

Random quick notes (to capture before I forget):
- PR #3821: check the aggregationMap merging logic — there was a nested loop that may produce combinatorial keys for models with many tags.
- Slack convo: #observability thread at 02:30 has a snippet from infra-alerts@pagerduty indicating high swap usage on node infra-11 — correlate.
- Possible workaround: temporarily disable "quantized" tag grouping in UI for heavy pages (low-friction config change).

To-do (personal):
- [ ] 09:30 — follow up with Taylor + CS update (short note)
- [ ] 10:00 — collect pod logs + attach to JIRA-OBS-2142
- [ ] 11:00 — test rollback staging (Emily) and report
- [ ] EOD — write short incident blurb for internal triage board if still unresolved

Open questions:
- Was there a scheduled job or nightly batch at 02:00 that increases cardinality? (Check cronjobs for model sync)
- Did recent model onboarding add a high-cardinality model tag set? (ask Model-Onboarding team)

References / links:
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Dashboard+Alerting+Runbook
- JIRA: JIRA-OBS-2142 (timeseries node OOMs), JIRA-OBS-2150 (UI fallback ticket)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/3821 (recent aggregation change)

---
End scratchpad — will prune and convert to JIRA notes once confirmed.
